title: NY State Senate · District 17
area: Southwest Brooklyn, including Bay Ridge, Bensonhurst, Dyker Heights and parts of Sunset Park.

context.text: Incumbent Steve Chan defeated Democratic incumbent Iwen Chu in the November 5, 2024 general election, flipping the seat. Both the Democratic and Republican primaries for this seat were canceled for 2026, with each candidate advancing unopposed to the general election.

summary.text: Steve Chan is the Republican, Conservative and "Stop Mamdani Party" candidate for NY State Senate District 17 in southwest Brooklyn. A Hong Kong-born retired NYPD sergeant and Marine Corps veteran, he defeated Democratic incumbent Iwen Chu in the November 2024 general election, flipping the seat. He is seeking a second term against Democrat Larry He.

background.text: Born in Hong Kong; immigrated to the United States at age 11 and settled in Bay Ridge, Brooklyn, where he has lived for 47 years, including 32 years in Bensonhurst.
Attended PS 102 in Bay Ridge, JHS 259 William McKinley, and Fort Hamilton High School, then SUNY Empire State College.
Served in the U.S. Marine Corps from 1984 to 1990.
Joined the NYPD in 1993 and retired as a sergeant in 2020 after 27 years.
Owned and operated a small florist shop in Sunset Park for 10 years and provided free notary services to neighbors.
Active in local schools as a school leadership team parent, Title I chairperson and PTA president; married with two daughters in public school.
Won the Republican and Conservative lines in 2024 without a primary and defeated incumbent Iwen Chu (D/WFP) in the November 2024 general election, taking office January 1, 2025.

In the 2025–2026 session was assigned to the Cities 1 Committee (ranking member), New York City Education Committee (ranking member), Education, Commerce, Economic Development and Small Business, and Investigations and Government Operations committees.

priorities.text: Describes himself as accessible rather than a career politician, saying he is fighting to stop what he calls decline in the city and state.
priorities.quote: I'm not a politician. I'm not looking for a job. I'm here to fight for us, our community, our city, our state. I'm here to stop the madness that is turning New York into dystopia.

priorities.text: Lists public safety, cashless bail, wasteful government spending, e-bike enforcement, illegal immigration, education, cost of living, health care, taxes, congestion pricing, and services for seniors and veterans as the issues he is focused on.
Says the first bill he would introduce is to provide qualified immunity for police officers.

record.text: Serves as ranking member on the Cities 1 and New York City Education committees; also serves on the Commerce, Economic Development and Small Business, Education, and Investigations and Government Operations committees.

Sponsored S9441, requiring landlords of one- to six-family rental dwellings in New York City to provide fire extinguishers in rented apartments; passed the Senate 60–0 on June 4, 2026 and remained pending in the Assembly Housing Committee.

Sponsored S10236, which would bar local governments from requiring businesses to replace existing storefront security gates or grilles solely for transparency or visual-access standards; remained in the Senate Consumer Protection Committee as of May 7, 2026.

Sponsored S10353, which would direct the Triborough Bridge and Tunnel Authority to discount Verrazano-Narrows Bridge tolls to 70% of the regular fare for Kings County residents using personal vehicles; remained in the Senate Transportation Committee as of May 14, 2026.

Sponsored S9938, which would impose mandatory prison sentences for certain offenses committed on public transportation and create a new felony offense of reckless endangerment on public transportation; remained in the Senate Codes Committee as of April 16, 2026.

summary.text: Larry He is the Democratic candidate for NY State Senate District 17 and a first-time candidate. He holds a Ph.D. in ecological economics, worked as a senior analyst at electric-grid operators, and is chief of staff to Assemblyman William Colton. His Ballotpedia survey lists safer and cleaner neighborhoods, affordable living and lower taxes, and faster, more accessible transit as his key messages.

background.text: Describes himself as a first-generation immigrant and a Democratic district leader.
Earned a Ph.D. in Ecological Economics from Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, where he also served as a student senator.
Worked as a senior analyst for the New York Independent System Operator and the California Independent System Operator, which oversee those states' electric power systems and electricity markets.
First worked for Assemblyman William Colton as an intern in 2006; in January 2024 Colton appointed him co-chief of staff, and his campaign now describes him as chief of staff.

In that role, according to his campaign website, he brings food pantries, neighborhood cleanups, senior services, legal assistance, immigration support, and small-business and nonprofit aid into the district.

Community roles listed by Colton's office include the National Governing Board of the Asian and Pacific Islanders American Public Affairs Association, board member of United Chinese Americans, board chair and president of the Chinese Community Center of the Capital Region of New York, and executive director of the Global Asian Carp Coalition.
Endorsed by Assemblyman William Colton and New York City Councilmember Susan Zhuang; this is his first run for public office.

priorities.text: Lists safer and cleaner neighborhoods, affordable living and lower taxes, and faster and more accessible transit as his three key campaign messages.
Says he is personally passionate about affordability, public safety, education and quality-of-life issues.

researchNotes: Larry He is a first-time candidate whose only substantial public statements found are his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey answers; no campaign website content beyond that survey, and no statements mapping to the fixed issue list, were found, so his positions list is empty rather than inferred. Chan's 2024 Patch Q&A lists priorities (including congestion pricing and illegal immigration) without a clear stance on the fixed-issue wording, and floor votes are compared separately, so no formal positions are included. Biography gap: Larry He's campaign materials do not give his birthplace or year of birth, and the district he serves as district leader is not stated in the sources found.
